title: How the hip and knee coordinate in walking: continuous relative phase and vector coding on real sagittal gait kinematics

dataset.name: A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics (WBDS)
dataset.record: 42 healthy adults, 3D motion capture; SAGITTAL hip and knee joint angles (RHipAngleZ, RKneeAngleZ) time-normalised to the gait cycle (101 points), overground and treadmill walking across speeds (328 treadmill + 123 overground trial-cycles used)
dataset.citation: Fukuchi CA, Fukuchi RK, Duarte M. A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics in healthy individuals. PeerJ 2018;6:e4640; data figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5722711 (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: Smoothness describes one joint; COORDINATION describes how two move together. On real SAGITTAL hip and knee angles the ecosystem recovers the same hip-knee coordination structure with two independent methods: continuous relative phase gives a mean absolute relative phase of 84 deg (the joints are substantially out of phase, not in lockstep), and vector coding finds the modal pattern is DISTAL / knee-led (0.36) with in-phase 0.29, proximal / hip-led 0.20 and anti-phase 0.15 -- the knee's large, fast swing excursion leading the smaller, slower hip arc. Two methods agree on the same structure.

validation.reference: The sagittal hip-knee angle-angle relationship is dominated by the knee: through swing the knee flexes and extends over a large (~60 deg) range while the hip moves through a smaller (~40 deg), slower arc, so the coordination is knee-led (distal) and the joints are substantially out of phase -- not simple in-phase lockstep. Two independent methods (continuous relative phase, giving MARP, and vector coding, giving the coupling-angle pattern proportions) must agree on this structure.
validation.data: REAL -- Fukuchi et al. 2018 (figshare 5722711), 42 subjects, 3D motion-capture SAGITTAL gait kinematics (RHipAngleZ / RKneeAngleZ)
validation.note: The reproducible result is the coordination STRUCTURE, on which two independent methods agree: MARP is a substantial 84 deg (out of phase, not in lockstep) and the modal vector-coding pattern is DISTAL / knee-led (0.36) -- the knee's dominant swing excursion leading the hip -- with in-phase 0.29, proximal 0.20 and anti-phase 0.15 (proportions sum to 1). INTEGRITY NOTE: an earlier version of this case used the RHipAngleX/RKneeAngleX columns, which in WBDS are the small-amplitude NON-sagittal components (~10-13 deg), not flexion/extension; the sagittal flexion is the Z axis (~40-68 deg). The corrected sagittal analysis gives the numbers above (the earlier 'in-phase-dominant, hip-led' reading was an axis artefact). The coordination VARIABILITY (deviation phase ~35 deg, coordination_variability.csv) is BETWEEN-trial/subject variability across the cohort and speeds, NOT stride-to-stride motor variability (which needs continuous multi-stride data this ensemble-cycle dataset lacks); treadmill and overground are similar (35.0 vs 34.0) precisely because the pooled measure is not cycle-to-cycle, so no condition difference is claimed.

open_questions.q: Cycle-to-cycle (stride-to-stride) coordination variability -- the motor-control marker elevated in injury and neurological disease -- needs continuous multi-stride joint-angle streams, which this ensemble-averaged dataset does not provide; validating it on real data awaits a continuous-gait kinematics source. Documented, not escalated.
